content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Warner Robins

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and project-management experience. Verify you meet the contact-hour and work-experience thresholds for PMP® candidacy. Review PMI's official eligibility criteria on their website, then contact Granite PM Academy if you have questions about your background.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Formal Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual PMP Bootcamp instructor-led course. Attend synchronous sessions from anywhere, covering all five process groups and ten knowledge areas. Receive your certificate of completion upon finishing, which you'll need for your PMI application.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: Create your PMI account and submit your PMP® application, including proof of your 35 contact hours and project-management experience. Pay the examination fee directly to PMI. Allow time for PMI to review and approve your application before scheduling your exam.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Take the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources, including practice tests and study guides, to reinforce bootcamp content. Schedule your exam with Pearson VUE. Sit for the computerized PMP® examination and receive your pass/fail result immediately upon completion.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP® Credential
steps_items.text: Your PMP® credential is valid for three years. Earn professional development units (PDUs) through approved PMI activities—training, volunteering, publishing, or presenting. Renew your credential before expiration by submitting your PDUs and paying the renewal fee to PMI.
